A filter chip is a button that is on or off: click it to fill it with a soft tint, click again to turn it off. Hover or Tab through the linked chips: the edge and words darken and focus shows the ring; the last chip in each row is static text and does not respond. Turn on With meta for a short detail after each name. No chip changes colour by state.

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river , and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To name one linked thing in a small, quiet label: a person, a team, a project, the record something belongs to.
  • As a link to that thing's page, or as static text when there is nowhere to go.
  • Several side by side, in a group that wraps onto as many lines as it needs.
  • With code, for an id people copy and trace exactly: an order number, an invoice number, a product code.

When not to use

  • To show the state of something: use cmp-status-pill. A chip carries no status colour, ever; colour with a word is the status pill's job (fdn-philosophy, principle 4).
  • For an action (Add, Remove, Filter): use cmp-button, quiet or secondary.
  • For a choice among a few options: use cmp-segmented-control or cmp-checkbox.
  • For a count or a category label in running text: use plain text (ds-text-caption).
  • For one link in a sentence: use a text link.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • default — a name in the base font: a person, a team, a project. The base class alone; no modifier class.
  • code — an id in the mono font, set exactly as it is written where it comes from: an order, an invoice, a product code.
  • filter — a small pill that is on or off, with an icon and a word: a <button type="button" aria-pressed>; off it is grey words on nothing, on it is filled with a soft tint of the spot colour, its words and icon in the spot colour. For the filters at the top of a list.

Anatomy

  • Root: <a class="ds-chip" href="…"> when it links somewhere; <span class="ds-chip"> when it only names. Add ds-chip--code for an id.
  • Meta (optional, with-meta): <span class="ds-chip__meta"> after the name, a muted detail such as a role or a count ("owner", "3 open").
  • Group: put several chips in a list, <ul class="ds-stack ds-stack--horizontal ds-stack--tight"> with one <li> per chip; the chip removes the list's bullets and indent, and the row wraps.
  • Every chip has the same quiet look: a hairline edge on the raised surface, muted words. Nothing about it says good or bad.

Accessibility

  • A linked chip is a plain link: its words are its accessible name, Tab reaches it and Enter follows it. A static chip is plain text and is not focusable.
  • A group of chips is a list, so screen readers hear how many there are; give it a name (aria-label) when the heading above it does not say what they are.
  • Words meet AA on the raised surface in every theme (text-muted on surface-raised).
  • A chip is at least 24 px tall and chips in a group sit apart, so each link can be hit on its own.

Interaction

  • A linked chip darkens its edge and words on hover within the quick duration; nothing grows or moves (int-01, int-03).
  • Focus draws the shared ring around the chip (int-02).
  • A static chip does not respond to hover or press.

Content rules

  • The name as it is everywhere else in the product, in its own case: "Billing", "Sam Rivera". An id exactly as it is written everywhere else, never shortened.
  • Meta is one to four words, comma-separated: "owner", "3 open".
  • Order chips the way the product lists them elsewhere, or alphabetically; never by importance shown in colour.

Do and don't

  • Do link a chip whenever the thing it names has a page.
  • Do keep all chips in one group the same variant: names, or ids.
  • Don't colour a chip to show a state, a result or a priority; use cmp-status-pill next to it.
  • Don't put a button or a second link inside a chip, or make a chip removable: an action beside it is a cmp-button.
